suspicions.claim: The unfollow DELETE query is missing the followed_id filter, causing it to delete all follow relationships for the follower instead of just the one for the specified user.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Create users A and B. 2. A follows B (POST /api/me/following/<B_id> as A). 3. A follows C (POST /api/me/following/<C_id> as A). 4. A unfollows B (DELETE /api/me/following/<B_id> as A). 5. Check A's following list (GET /api/me/following as A). Observe that C is no longer followed (data missing C).
suspicions.evidence: Probe 'probe s1: user_alice' and 'probe_s1' show DELETE /api/me/following/2 returned 204 in both base and head, but subsequent GET /api/me/following returned followed user Carol (id 3) in base and empty list in head, confirming unfollow deleted all follow relationships.

suspicions.claim: Unfollowing a user that the current user does not follow incorrectly returns 204 No Content instead of 409 Conflict, because the is_following check was removed from the model method.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Create users A and B. 2. Ensure A does NOT follow B. 3. A attempts to unfollow B (DELETE /api/me/following/<B_id> as A). 4. Read response status code. Observe 204 instead of expected 409.
suspicions.evidence: Probe 'probe_s2' shows DELETE /api/me/following/1 (unfollowing non-followed user) returned 204 in both base and head, so the behavior did not change.

suspicions.claim: The unfollow endpoint returns 204 No Content even when the target user does not exist, because the model method no longer validates the relationship and the route's user lookup may be bypassed or the delete executes silently on non-existent followed_id.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Authenticate as user A. 2. Send DELETE /api/me/following/99999 (non-existent user ID). 3. Read response status code. Observe 204 instead of expected 404.
suspicions.evidence: Probe 'probe_s3' shows DELETE /api/me/following/99999 (non-existent user) returned 404 in both base and head, so the behavior did not change.
